# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can only feel three wire positions and have no tactile labels or other details. The useful route is for Deaf to speak visual observations aloud, which I can hear; Mute can prompt Deaf with visible gestures. I will ask Mute to do that and directly gesture a “you, call/speak” request toward Deaf.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I feel only three unlabeled wire positions. Please gesture Deaf to speak aloud every visual detail: wire colors, labels, markings, lights, and display. I can hear Deaf's speech.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤙"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state: display 8; light green; wires in positions one red, two yellow, three blue. Mute sent gesture rules apparently indexed by display values 4, 7, and 8.

The visible configuration is now known, but I still lack the manual’s rule for display 8. Mute’s gestured rules reached Deaf, who can translate their meaning into speech for me. I will ask Deaf for the exact instruction associated with 8 and wait rather than cut.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝", "✌", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute confirms the rule for display 8. Its instruction is the three gestures: OK sign, thumbs-down, then Vulcan salute. No action has been performed. Visible state is still green light; wires red, yellow, blue in positions 1, 2, 3.

The manual instruction for 8 has reached Deaf only as gesture symbols, and I cannot infer a cut position from those symbols alone. No action should be taken until Deaf translates the rule into a wire position, using the visible wire colours and Mute’s manual information.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please ask Deaf, by gesture, to speak aloud what the display-8 gesture sequence means in terms of the visible wires: specifically which numbered wire I must cut. Do not authorize a cut until that is stated.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visual change: display 8, green light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute’s display-8 instruction is exactly: OK, thumbs-down, Vulcan salute. Please use your manual to translate it before acting.

Mute has heard Deaf’s spoken visual state, so Mute should now be able to apply the manual. The three gesture symbols are not themselves an actionable cut instruction for me. I will ask Mute to send Deaf one unambiguous numbered-wire answer, so Deaf can speak that number to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="You have Deaf's spoken state: display 8, green, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Apply the manual and gesture Deaf a single unambiguous cut-wire number: one finger for wire 1, two fingers for wire 2, or three fingers for wire 3. Deaf, please speak that number aloud to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Still unchanged: display 8, green light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute repeats display-8 code: OK, thumbs-down, Vulcan salute. Mute then sends these additional symbols exactly: pointing-at-you, writing hand, right-pointing hand, index-up, victory sign, I-love-you hand. Interpret via the manual before acting.

Mute alone can apply the manual, and Deaf can see Mute’s gestures and speak their identity to me. The added sequence appears to be further encoded material rather than a clear numeric answer. I will establish a simple final-answer convention: send Deaf exactly one numeric hand sign and nothing else—☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3—then Deaf reports it aloud. I will not cut until that arrives.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please now give the final manual-derived cut choice only. Gesture Deaf exactly ONE of these and no other symbol: ☝ means cut wire 1; ✌ means cut wire 2; 🤟 means cut wire 3. Deaf: speak the one received symbol's wire number aloud.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visual change. Mute has now sent only an index-up gesture. Please signal, using the established gesture vocabulary, whether you have identified the required physical action from the manual; do not act unless the instruction is clear.

Mute sent only the established index-up final-answer sign, which means cut wire 1. Deaf has confirmed that this is the sole final signal. I will cut wire position 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
